summary: A 1930 St. Augustine Record report describes an 80-foot steel observation tower at Mill Creek, St. Johns County; its later history is not in any source found.

events.note: Reported completed the week before 13 Nov 1930; the tower was 80 feet (24 m) tall steel.

evidence.supports: built 1930; 80-foot steel observation tower completed the week before 13 Nov 1930
evidence.quote: The eighty-foot steel observation tower located at Mill Creek, thirteen miles west of St. Augustine on the Green Cove Springs road, was completed last week.

evidence.supports: county farm agent E. H. Vance reported the plan; federal government to build and maintain tower and ranger station (May 1930)
evidence.quote: the federal government will build and maintain a fire observation tower and forest ranger station here

evidence.supports: tower about a mile from the school house
evidence.quote: The tower will be located in the Mill Creek section approximately a mile from the present school house.
J. K. Malphurs has been named as the ranger

evidence.supports: some 90,000 acres listed as a protective unit with the Florida Forest Service
evidence.quote: A section of St. Johns County comprising some 90,000 acres is listed as a fire protective unit with the Florida Forest Service

evidence.supports: lookout to be kept in the tower in fire season
evidence.quote: A lookout will be retained in the tower during the fire season to detect forest fires.

evidence.supports: phone line to five crews, 27 miles
evidence.quote: He will be connected to five fire fighting crews by twenty-seven miles of telephone line.

evidence.supports: landowners and state and federal governments contributed four cents an acre
evidence.quote: The landowners and the state and federal governments have combined by contributing a total of four cents an acre in an effort to control forest fires.

evidence.supports: public invited to visit the tower in 1930
evidence.quote: Visitors are cordially invited to visit the tower.

evidence.supports: county farm agent E. H. Vance reported the plan (clipping of May 27, 1930)
evidence.quote: E. H. Vance, county farm agent, reported today

evidence.supports: September 1930 clipping date (90,000 acres listed; ranger named)
reported in the St. Augustine Record

sources.title: Mill Creek - Forest Lookouts (1930 St. Augustine Record clippings)

notes_for_editor: LOCATION CONFLICT, needs a human check: the record point (30.26451, -83.28404) is roughly 190 km west of St. Augustine, but the 1930 report places the tower 13 miles (21 km) west of St. Augustine on the Green Cove Springs road. No correction is written because no source gives a corrected point. The record's county is blank; the sources say St. Johns County. The brief's source page (mill-creek.html) shows only the heading in the copy I read; the 1930 clippings are on mill-creek1.html, which is the URL cited here, so the source_pages list should be updated. Agency: the May and September 1930 clippings link the protective unit to the Florida Forest Service; the operator of the tower itself is not named. The May clipping says the federal government would build and maintain the tower, and the November clipping credits the landowners and state and federal governments with funding; these are plans and funding, not a conflict. Nothing after 1930 was found in one extra search (no later use, removal or site description). Height is 80 feet as a total tower height as reported; height_m is not set because the cab-floor height is not given. No photos found.
